import sys

def solve():
    # Read first line
    line = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip('\n')
    # Find the first token (integer)
    tokens = line.split()
    if not tokens:
        return
    n = int(tokens[0])
    # Get the rest of the line after the integer token (including leading spaces)
    idx = line.index(tokens[0])
    rest = line[idx + len(tokens[0]):]
    # The string to process is the rest of the line (may be empty)
    s = rest

    inside = False
    inside_words = 0
    max_outside = 0
    current_len = 0

    # Process first n characters of s (if s is shorter, index error will occur, matching Java behavior)
    for i in range(n):
        c = s[i]
        if c == '(':
            if current_len > 0:
                if inside:
                    inside_words += 1
                elif current_len > max_outside:
                    max_outside = current_len
                current_len = 0
            inside = True
        elif c == ')':
            if current_len > 0:
                if inside:
                    inside_words += 1
                elif current_len > max_outside:
                    max_outside = current_len
                current_len = 0
            inside = False
        elif c == '_':
            if current_len > 0:
                if inside:
                    inside_words += 1
                elif current_len > max_outside:
                    max_outside = current_len
                current_len = 0
        else:
            current_len += 1

    # Final flush
    if current_len > 0:
        if inside:
            inside_words += 1
        elif current_len > max_outside:
            max_outside = current_len

    print(max_outside, inside_words)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    solve()
